frames.narration: A customer pays a merchant 20.00. The payment service asks the ledger to post one entry with the key pay-501: debit the customer's wallet 2,000 cents, credit the merchant 1,940 and credit the fee account 60. The API adds up the lines: 2,000 minus 1,940 minus 60 is zero, so the entry is balanced.
The API checks the key. pay-501 has not been seen before, so the entry goes on. The fee line is sent to fees#3, one of 8 sub-accounts, so that the busy fee account does not become one locked row.

In one database transaction the three lines are appended to the journal as entry 8,812, the key is stored with it, and the three balance rows are moved by their amounts. The transaction commits, so all of it is visible together.
The payment service did not hear the answer, so it retries with the same key. The lookup finds entry 8,812, writes nothing, and returns it. The customer is charged once.
The entry goes onto the stream in order. Statements, reports and the warehouse read it from there, and none of them can change it.

At night the reconciler replays the journal for the wallet and compares it with the stored balance. Both say 31,000 and the sum of all balances is zero. It also matches the merchant's bank payout to the credit of 1,940 by reference.

The customer is refunded. The journal is not edited. A new entry 8,930 with the key rev-8812 negates every line of entry 8,812 and points to it. The wallet goes back to 33,000, and both entries stay on the record. A second click on refund finds the key and does nothing.
